subject: EdgeBridge private pool throughput & routing tradeoffs — sizing review
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgebridge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeBridge private pool throughput & routing tradeoffs — sizing review

Alex — thanks again for the deep dive earlier. Per our call, I wanted to capture a focused set of questions and a proposed sizing starting point so your infra team can validate constraints before we finalize procurement numbers. Attaching a draft capacity model and a simple network diagram.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm peak sustained QPS target (tokens/s) for the inference endpoint during your expected 3-hour evening window.
- Confirm acceptable P95/P99 latency envelopes (we proposed P95 < 120ms, P99 < 350ms at 2048 token context).
- Any hard egress limits or peering windows on the VPC side (egress caps in Mbps per AZ).

High-level sizing recommendation (draft):
- Start: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved slab) with 2 warm standby hosts for burst absorption.
- Admission: 90% admission for mixed chat + embeddings traffic; at 95th percentile use shard-level routing to cheaper quantized variant.
- Network: 40Gbps per host aggregate to meet KV cache replication and model weight loading during burst.

Attachments: edgebridge_capacity_model.xlsx (tabbed: workload, sizing, cost), network_topology_diagram.png (BGP/peering + VPC NAT), mutual_action_plan.md (deliverables + timelines).

Can your ops folks validate the QPS target and any hard egress caps by EOD Monday? If those numbers line up we'll lock the committed slab sizing and move to contract.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: EdgeBridge private pool throughput & routing tradeoffs — sizing review

Marissa — appreciate the clear summary and the workbook. I ran the draft by our infra lead (cc'd Ops) and here are the main constraints from our side:

1) Peak: our evening batch window currently hits ~2.1k QPS for small-response completions (avg 120 tokens); however we expect a product change in Q1 that increases average tokens to ~400 for 30% of requests. Please size for two scenarios (current and +Q1 payload).
2) Latency: P95 target of 150ms is acceptable as a business SLA (we're mostly conversational flows). P99 we cannot exceed 500ms for SLA reasons.
3) Egress caps: our carrier contract limits egress per AZ to 18Gbps sustained; is your suggested 40Gbps per host an absolute requirement or a conservative upper bound?

Op note: we need the cold-start model load profile too — large model warmup IO could make host-level 40Gbps necessary if we can't preheat KV cache before traffic.

We'll validate exact VPC peering CIDR allocations Monday and send the confirmed numbers. Attached Ops will drop a short note with their network test plan.

Thanks — Alex

Subject: Re: EdgeBridge private pool throughput & routing tradeoffs — sizing review

Alex / team — I reviewed the workbook and sketched an alternate configuration for the Q1 payload increase that trades network for GPU headroom. Summary:

- Scenario A (current): 16 GPUs, 2 warm standbys, per-host 20Gbps network. Use aggressive prefix KV caching and admission control to keep warmup IO low.
- Scenario B (Q1 heavier payload): 24 GPUs, 4 standbys, per-host 25-40Gbps depending on whether you allow pre-mounted NVMe for checkpoint staging. If egress per-AZ is capped at 18Gbps then we need to spread instances across additional AZs and use cross-AZ KV cache replication with async preheat (adds ~30ms p95 overhead).

Operational notes:
- Warmup: If you can tolerate a ~60s window of slightly elevated latency during deploys we can avoid 40Gbps per-host by doing rolling preloads and keeping a small hot-slab with the most frequent shards.
- Routing: We'll implement model-variant fallback: quantized 8-bit variant for non-critical calls. That reduces GPU/time by ~28% but increases P99 variance slightly.

I'll attach a short table in the workbook with the tradeoffs; shipping that now. Happy to walk Ops through a short test plan (iperf + synthetic KV access patterns) to validate whether your carrier truly enforces 18Gbps.

-rishi

Thanks everyone — good set of clarifications. Agreement summary and next steps (mutual action plan):

1) EdgeBridge to confirm by EOD Tuesday: true sustained egress cap per AZ and confirmed Q1 payload mix (% of heavy requests). (Action: EdgeBridge Ops)
2) Redwood to produce final pricing for two committed slabs: (A) 16-GPU reserved slab w/ 2 warm standbys (Baseline) and (B) 24-GPU reserved slab w/ 4 standby hosts (Q1-ready). Deliverable: final quote + SLO annex. (Action: Redwood Sales/Finance)
3) Joint test plan: 72-hour soak in staging with iperf network tests and synthetic KV access pattern. Redwood to provide test harness; EdgeBridge to run in their staging VPC. (Action: Redwood Eng + EdgeBridge Ops)
4) Contract milestone: upon successful soak and confirmation of egress numbers, execute reserved capacity contract (deal EB-2026-0412). Target sign: Nov 30, 2026.

Attachments updated: mutual_action_plan.md (live) — I added timeline bullets and acceptance criteria. I've also attached the workbook with Rishi's scenario table included.

If Purchasing needs a simplified one-page appendix for internal approval, let me know and I can draft it today.

Best — Marissa
